The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d8e092ab0484f8b9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 20-21. statement: From every sequence of admissible sizes tending to infinity one can extract a subsequence along which ( νn, mn, (Mn,k)k≥1 ) =⇒ ( ν, m, (Mk)k≥1 ) jointly, in the local vague topology for the point measures and the compact-open topology on the upper half-plane for the analytic functions. The limiting point measure ν = ∑ j δxj is locally finite, 20 with multiplicities permitted. There are deterministic ξ, χ > 0, depending only on d, E, such that the following properties hold. For every fixed 0 < δ < 1, almost surely for all sufficiently large R, m(e + iu) = m∗ + O(u−ξ ), |e| ≤ R, Rδ ≤ u ≤ R2 , (4.13) and, almost surely, ν([v, w]) = ρ(w − v) + O(R1−χ ), −R ≤ v ≤ w ≤ R, R −→ ∞. (4.14) The constants and starting values of R in these almost sure statements may depend on the sample and on δ, but the exponents are deterministic. On a possible extension of the probability space, for every fixed k there are standard Gaussian vectors gj ∈ R2k, independent over j conditionally on ν, such that m(z) = mr + PV ∑ j 1 xj − z , Mk(z) = Kk(mr) + PV ∑ j C 1/2 k gjgT j C 1/2 k xj − z . (4.15) These representations are consistent as k increases by retaining the first k edge channels. A separate Gaussian mark is assigned to each occurrence of a repeated point. The principal values converge locally uniformly on the upper half-plane, and ℑMk(z) is positive definite there, almost surely simultaneously for every finite k and every z with ℑz > 0.
